title: Sometimes the road ahead seams like it goes on forever.
alt: Sometimes the road ahead seams like it goes on forever.
excerpt: Sometimes the road ahead seams like it goes on forever. There’s a trail by my home where I walk often and it’s stretches on for miles and miles. As I look forward to see how the trail nev...
body: Sometimes the road ahead seams like it goes on forever. There’s a trail by my home where I walk often and it’s stretches on for miles and miles. As I look forward to see how the trail never ends, I think I can’t do it. It feels exhausting and my feet feel like they’re trudging through quicksand. Think on your life with how overwhelmed you can become when you realize what you still need to achieve and how far away it feels. The heaviness is real. The impossibility of the journey feels wildly obvious. When you see how far you still have to go, you feel defeated and doubt creeps into your mind. I know the old saying goes, “Don’t look back, you are not going that way.” But I have to confess, looking back is what lately has propelled me forward with greater momentum and resolve. The vision of the mountains I’ve already climbed. The empty valleys I’ve surrendered in and laid flat on my face, wishing for hope. I’ve found myself in forests where tree after tree made it impossible to see the way out and I felt that it would be the thing that would finally break me. But…. I kept crawling. I kept wandering, I climbed and climbed until I reached a point where I could see with clarity the way out and beyond. I marveled at how far I had already come. So I’m changing the saying! “Don’t look back too long, you’re not going that way.  But DO look back with a smile, knowing how hard you fought to get where you are.” Then let that fire keep burning inside of you, so you can go get what you want!”

title: You are not their savior.
alt: Typography graphic reading 'You are not their savior.'
excerpt: We are called to reflect Christ, not replace Him. Love and support are holy. Control is not.
body:
One of the wisest things a good friend ever said to me was “My kids have a Savior and it’s not me.” I sat with that for a while.

In my need to control outcomes to avoid pain, I’ve felt this responsibility to carry and take upon myself the entirety of people’s pain, struggles, and even shelter them from the consequences of their own choices. I’ve learned in the process that, that doesn’t empower them, it breaks them.

Trying to take those things from a person takes away God’s opportunity to teach them the lessons that could eventually lead them to recognize their complete need for reliance on their Savior. We can’t force people to change anything about their character or choices. Our power to strengthen and love them comes from our own trust in God’s perfect timing and understanding.

Stop drowning from others’ issues, when you have a Savior who can teach them to swim. Prayers are important. Love and support are important. Control is not. It was never ours to begin with.

title: The human heart has one maker.
alt: Painting-style image of Jesus embracing a woman with text about the human heart.
excerpt: You can seek thrill, joy, or pleasure and still discover that the feeling of completeness is missing. There is a good reason for that.
body:
You can seek thrill, joy, or pleasure and you can find it for a time. Even for a long time....its offered by people, places, and things.

Although, at some point you may recognize you don’t feel whole. You aren’t at peace. The feeling of completeness is missing.

There’s a good reason for that. 💕

title: Replaceable everywhere except here.
alt: Illustration of a mother holding a baby with the words 'I'm replaceable everywhere except here.'
excerpt: There’s no achievement so great that it could hold a flame to the sense of purpose and value found in being a mother to my precious kids.
body:
There’s no achievement so great or anything I could ever possess that could hold a flame to the sense of purpose and true value I feel in being a mother to my precious kids.

I was scared to be a mom. 18 years ago I looked down at this little person in my arms and thought.... “I’m so far from perfect and some days it feels like I can hardly keep myself together. I’m supposed to raise this human and teach them all of these life skills and values and make sure they grow up to be good people?”

My answer to myself was a fearful but firm, “yes!” There have been a million reasons and times where my heart has been heavy and I’ve felt doubt in my influence or power to inspire them for good. Yet, as I scroll through years worth of pictures and memories...I am humbled that I got to have the best privilege placed upon my shoulders.

I would start over and go through all of the hard, painful, and ugly over and over again if it meant that I could witness all of the deep goodness and love that these precious people possess. I know each of their hearts. I’ve seen their hardships and struggles. They’ve taught me more than I could have ever gained from a million hours of lessons, classes, or training. No matter what choices they make or who they choose to become, they have my loyalty and the love of my whole heart forever. Nothing could shake that.
